name: Baingan Bharta
subtitle: fire-roasted aubergine mashed rough with onion and tomato, smoky throughout

image.alt: Baingan bharta, smoked mashed aubergine with spring onion

ingredients.qty: 2 large (900g total), the fat round purple kind
6 cloves, minced, plus 4 whole cloves for roasting
3 tbsp, heated to smoking and cooled

prepNotes: Choose aubergines that feel light for their size. Those have fewer seeds and roast sweeter.
Make four small slits in each aubergine and push a whole garlic clove into each, then rub the skin with oil.
Roast directly over a gas flame if you can. The smoke is the point of the dish and an oven cannot fully replace it.

steps.text: Set the aubergines directly on a medium gas flame and roast 15 to 20 minutes, turning every few minutes with tongs.
steps.tip: It is done when the skin is blistered black all over and the whole thing sags like a deflated balloon.

steps.text: If you have no gas flame, roast at 240C for 45 minutes, turning twice, then blacken briefly under the grill.
Put the roasted aubergines in a covered bowl for 10 minutes. The steam loosens the skin.
Peel off every scrap of charred skin, then chop and mash the flesh roughly with a fork.
steps.tip: Do not rinse the flesh under the tap. You will wash the smoke straight down the drain.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and fry on medium-high for 10 minutes until deep gold.
Stir in the ginger, minced garlic and green chillies and fry 2 minutes.
Add the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt, and cook 10 minutes until the tomato disappears into a thick masala and oil separates.
Fold in the mashed aubergine and cook 8 minutes on medium, pressing and stirring, until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan.
steps.tip: Keep the texture uneven. Bharta should never be smooth.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala and most of the coriander, taste for salt, and finish with the rest of the coriander.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and the smokiness holds up well. Reheat in a pan, not a microwave. Freezes 2 months.
